items.subject: Petition under Section 62 read with Section 79(1)(d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 and under Regulations 15(1)(a) and 23 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 read with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 for determination cum truing up of the transmission tariff for the 2019-24 period and under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 for determination of the transmission tariff for the 2024- 29 period for the assets under North Eastern Region Strengthening Scheme XII. Petition under Section 62 read with Section 79(1)(d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 and under Regulations 15(1)(a) and 23 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 read with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 for determination cum truing up of the transmission tariff for the 2019-24 period and under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 for determination of the transmission tariff for the 2024- 29 period for the assets under North Eastern Region Strengthening Scheme XII.

**4. Power and Electricity Department,** Government of Mizoram, Aizawl. (Mizoram).

- _a) “Approve the determination cum trued-up Transmission Tariff for 2019-24 block and transmission tariff for 2024-29 block for the assets covered under this petition, as per para 24 and 25 above._

- b) _Admit the capital cost claimed and additional capitalization incurred during 2019-24 and also allow the projected additional capitalization during 2024-29._

- e) _Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulations, 2019 and Tariff Regulations, 2024 as per para 24 & 25 above for respective block._

- f) _Approve the reimbursement of expenditure by the beneficiaries towards petition filing fee, and expenditure on publishing of notices in newspapers in terms of 70(1) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 and Regulation 94 (1) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024, and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of petition._

- g) _Allow the petitioner to bill and recover RLDC fees & charges and Licensee fee, separately from the respondents in terms of Regulation 70 (3) and (4) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 and Regulation 94 (3) and (4) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024._

- h) _Allow the petitioner to bill and adjust impact on Interest on Loan due to change in Interest rate on account of floating rate of interest applicable during 201924 and 2024-29 period, if any, from the respondents._

- j) _Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses as mentioned at para 31 above._

- k) _Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the overall insurance expenses and consequential IOWC on that insurance expenses as mentioned at para 31 above._

- l) _Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the overall capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual as mentioned at Para 31 above._

- m) _Allow the petitioner to claim expenses of CTUIL borne by POWERGRID through a separate petition on year to year/ at the end of tariff block as mentioned at para 32 above._

- n) _Allow the Petitioner to bill and recover GST on Transmission Charges separately from the respondents, if GST on transmission is levied at any rate in future. Further, any taxes including GST and duties including cess, etc. imposed by any statutory/Govt./municipal authorities shall be allowed to be recovered from the beneficiaries._

- _o) Condone the delay in completion of subject assets on merit of the same beyond the control of Petitioner in line with CERC Regulations, 2019 22(2) “uncontrollable factors” and approve the tariff as claimed._

_and pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_

3. During the hearing on 22.4.2026, the Petitioner's representative submitted that the cost claimed for the reconductoring works in the present Petition had already been claimed as Additional Capital Expenditure (ACE) under the original projects in Petition No. 529/TT/2025 (Chukha Transmission System) and Petition No. 509/TT/2025 (Transmission System associated with Loktak HEP). Accordingly, sought permission to withdraw the instant Petition.

4. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions and perused the record. It is noted that the Commission, vide order dated 25.10.2024 in Petition No. 94/TT/2024, observed that the capital expenditure incurred for re-conductoring shall be claimed as Additional Capitalisation under the transmission system where the original transmission line was initially approved.

5. In instant case, the Petitioner, by its affidavits dated 18.2.2026 and 13.5.2026, has submitted that the original transmission lines relating to the

transmission assets in this case were covered in two Petitions, namely (i) Petition No. 529/TT/2025 (Chukha Transmission System) and (ii) Petition No. 509/TT/2025 (Transmission System associated with Loktak HEP), in which the costs of the reconductoring works have already been claimed as Additional Capitalisation under the respective original projects. Accordingly, the Petitioner prayed for the withdrawal of this Petition.

6. Considering the submissions made by the Petitioner`s representative, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw this Petition.

items.subject: Approval of tariff for Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station, Unit-I (250 MW) for the period 2016-19 - Implementation of the APTEL judgment dated 19.11.2024 in Appeal No. 137/2019 (NTPC v CERC & ors). NTPC Limited
items.pdf_digest:
With regard to the prayer of the Petitioner for condonation of time overrun for the period from April 2013 to January 2015, on account of violence and bandh in the concerned area/region, the Commission, in its order dated 22.5.2017 (in Petition No.45/GT/2016), held as under:

_“20. As regards time over-run due to violence and bandhs during the period from April, 2013 to January, 2015, petitioner has requested to condone the delay of 671 days and has furnished the copy of the various prohibitory orders, but the same does not indicate the exact date of imposition of prohibitory orders. The petitioner has also submitted the supporting document indicating the prohibition from 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 (i.e. 32 days). Though, the petitioner was directed to submit the effective duration of bandh against prohibitory orders, the petitioner has not submitted the same and therefore, we are inclined to condone the delay of only 32 days. Based on the above discussion, the total delay of 32 days has been condoned, out of the delay of 671 days claimed by the petitioner.”_

_“18. ….. Accordingly, on analysis of such prohibitory orders, the delay of 32 days (from 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014) was condoned in order dated 22.5.2017. The Commission having considered the documents furnished by the petitioner with regard to violence and bandhs while allowing the time overrun in order dated 22.5.2017, we find no reason to entertain the petitioner’s plea for review of the said order on this issue. Accordingly, there is no error apparent on the face of the order dated 22.5.2017 and therefore the prayer of the petitioner for review on this ground fails.”_

_19. Hence, the findings of the commission on this issue are absolutely erroneous and unjustified, which cannot be sustained. The same are hereby set aside. We remand the matter back to the Commission to decide the issue afresh after hearing the parties and in the light of whole bunch of documents filed by the appellant, as noted hereinabove.”_

4. In the remand proceedings, the Petitioner, on the issue of time overrun for the period from April 2013 to January, 2015 on account of violence and Bandhs in the concerned area/region, had submitted the following:

_“As regards the issue (a)-time overrun for the period from April, 2013 to January, 2015 (671 days) on account of ethnic violence and bandh in the concerned area, the Commission had refused to condone the delay for the said period, except the period of 32 days, citing non-submission of prohibitory orders by NTPC during the time period in question. However, the APTEL has held that the Commission had taken note of only one page, which bears details of Section 144 prohibitory orders enforced between 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 and thus condoned the delay of these 32 days only. Whereas, the Petitioner had provided several other documents to support its claim that the project work was seriously impeded on account of violence and bandh from April 2013 to January 2015, but the same has not been considered._

_The APTEL in para 17 of its judgment has also held that the situation in Kokrajhar District, where the power project was being constructed, remained volatile and affected by regular bandhs/curfew/prohibitory orders etc., throughout the years 2013-15, and the situation returned to normal in January 2015. The finding of APTEL is amply clear that the situation in Kokrajhar remained volatile for the complete period of the dispute (2013-15) and therefore, the delay on account of ethnic violence and bandh of 671 days, during this period, is to be condoned, considering the overlapping period”_

## _5._ However, the Commission, after examining the aforesaid submissions, including the documents filed by the Petitioner for the said period, vide order 20.11.2025, held as under:

_“27. The Petitioner has further submitted that the project construction activities were affected due to the unrest, violence, etc. caused in the Kokrajhar district, where the project is located and has also provided the documents indicating the time overrun, progress bar chart, etc., for the activities affected. As submitted by the Petitioner, due to the poor law and order situation and bandh calls, in the Kokrajhar area, the workers had not turned up for work or were available in small numbers, which had a cascading effect, as the work on all fronts came to a near halt. In addition, the movement of goods and vehicles was affected during the bandh. Also, these disturbances/law and order issues have disrupted the normal project operations, thereby leading to significant delays in the project development activities. Thus, the participation of the various groups in bandhs, resulted in_

_28. As stated, the Petitioner, in Appendix-A has also submitted a tabular statement_

_indicating the date of the prohibitory order and the period of enforcement/revocation, during the period 2013-2015, which works out to a delay of 550 days, inclusive of the delay of 32 days allowed for the period 2.5.2014 to 2.6.2014 vide Commission’s order dated 22.5.2017. In consideration of the above submissions and the documents available on record, we condone the total delay of 550 days (which is inclusive of the 32 days delay already allowed vide order dated 22.5.2017), for the period 2013-15, after adjusting the overlapping period, since the said delays, due to violence/riots/ incidents relating to NDBF/Bandhs and Prohibitory orders, in Kokrajhar district, were all beyond the control of the Petitioner. In other words, for the period 2013-15, an additional delay of 518 days (55032) has been allowed in this order, in terms of the submissions/documents, and based on the findings of the APTEL judgment.”_
